entries.answer_en: Not out of the box, and I would say that plainly. General models are stronger on Modern Standard Arabic than on Gulf dialects. Mixing Arabic and English in one sentence is where many systems break. I would measure on real calls first, then decide.
entries.followup_en: Options after the number: fine-tune on our recordings, add a custom vocabulary for names, or a correction layer for common misses. A low-confidence line should ask the user to confirm. Promising 99 percent on Emirati plus English without a labelled set would be dishonest.
entries.answer_ar: اللهجة الإماراتية ومزج الإنجليزية لن تعمل جاهزة؛ أقيس على محادثات حقيقية ثم أضبط أو أطلب تأكيداً عند ضعف الثقة.

entries.question: What do you do with the audio recordings after processing?
aliases: what do you do with the audio recordings after processing
do you store the audio
how do you handle privacy of voice data
how long do you keep recordings
is a voice personal data
who can replay a call
entries.answer_en: My default is delete the audio and keep the text, unless there is a written reason to keep it. A voice is personal data. I also redact IDs spoken in the transcript. If the business needs audio for disputes, it is encrypted, rare access, every play logged.
entries.followup_en: Retention is a job in the system, not a person remembering to delete. In the kiosk I did not need long-term recordings to answer a visitor. Storing raw audio 'just in case' is a leak waiting. Policy first, then the folder permissions.
entries.answer_ar: الأصل حذف التسجيل وإبقاء النص بعد حجب المعرّفات، وإن لزم الصوت للنزاعات يُشفَّر ويُقيَّد الوصول مع سجل.

entries.question: How would you deploy an AI system in an on-premise production environment?
aliases: how would you deploy an ai system on premise
how do you deploy a model to production
what does your production architecture look like
how would you put an llm system into production
docker compose for llm
what sits in front of the model server
entries.answer_en: I would put the API, model server, and vector store in Docker, and cache repeated answers. The model sits behind one OpenAI-style URL so we can swap engines. I add latency and cost metrics on day one. I have not used vLLM in production; I would use it to keep the GPU busy.
entries.followup_en: A first build can be one or two GPU boxes with Compose, Redis, and a reverse proxy. Kubernetes can wait. Secrets stay out of images. I have run on-prem payments, not a GPU farm, so on the first GPU install I would pair with infra. Monitoring is how we notice a silent cost spike.
entries.answer_ar: أنشر الخدمة والنموذج ومخزن المتجهات في حاويات خلف واجهة واحدة، مع كاش ومقاييس من اليوم الأول، وأؤجّل كوبرنتس إن لم نحتجه.

entries.question: How would you reduce the running cost of an LLM system?
aliases: how would you reduce the running cost
how do you control llm costs
how do you make the system cheaper to run
what will this cost us per month
how do you cache llm answers
small model for easy questions
entries.answer_en: Caching the same internal question is the biggest win. Simple questions go to a small model; hard ones go to a large one. A serving engine batches GPU work. Caps on output length and per-user rate stop silent growth. I measure cost per request before I tune.
entries.followup_en: I have not used vLLM in production; I would use it for that batching. Prompt bloat is a tax: extra retrieved chunks you do not need. Streaming does not save money but it makes wait feel cheaper. A monthly bill without a per-call metric is guessing.
entries.answer_ar: أخفض التكلفة بكاش الأسئلة المتكررة، وتوجيه السهل لنموذج صغير، ودفعات على البطاقة، وحدود للطول والمعدل بعد قياس تكلفة الطلب.

entries.question: Why Docker? What problem does it actually solve?
aliases: why docker
what problem does docker solve
do you know docker
why containerize the model service
it works on my machine
entries.answer_en: It fixes 'it works on my machine'. The container carries the app, the language version, and the libraries, so laptop and server behave the same. AI stacks are fragile; a CUDA mismatch can break everything. A bad release rolls back by running the previous image.
entries.followup_en: Images also make air-gap transfer possible: build and scan outside, copy in, run. I still keep GPU driver contracts documented. Docker is not security by itself. It is repeatability. Compose is enough until we outgrow one host.
entries.answer_ar: دوكر يوحّد التشغيل بين جهازي والخادم مع المكتبات، وهذا حاسم في الذكاء الاصطناعي لأن اختلاف CUDA يكفي لتعطيل الخدمة.

entries.question: What is a container, and how is it different from a virtual machine?
aliases: what is a container
container versus virtual machine
docker versus vm
what is the difference between a container and a vm
why are containers lighter
do we still need vms
entries.answer_en: A container packages the app and its libraries and shares the host kernel, so it is light and starts fast. A VM carries a full operating system. Heavier, slower, stronger isolation. I put AI services in containers. The platform team may still park those containers on VMs.
entries.followup_en: For a ministry, VMs can be the tenancy boundary; containers are the deploy unit. Mixing GPUs on one kernel needs clear device rules. I do not pretend a container equals a VM sandbox. I use each for what it is good at.
entries.answer_ar: الحاوية تغلف التطبيق وتشارك نواة المضيف فهي أخف، والجهاز الافتراضي يحمل نظاماً كاملاً لعزل أقوى.

entries.question: Our environment is fully air-gapped. How would you build in it?
aliases: our environment is air gapped, how would you build in it
how do you deploy without internet access
how do you work in an isolated network
how do you bring models into a closed network
internal package mirror
how do you transfer model weights
entries.answer_en: The model file is the easy part. The hard part is the supply chain. I build and scan images outside, then bring them in with a checksum. Inside we need a registry and a package mirror so nothing reaches the public internet. Licenses get checked before we depend on a cloud-only tool.
entries.followup_en: Weights are huge, so the transfer procedure is an architecture item. After copy we verify the hash. Build-time pip install from the internet will fail, and that failure should happen in CI outside, not on the ministry box. I have lived this pattern in payment networks, not yet with GPU models.
entries.answer_ar: في شبكة معزولة تُبنى الصور وتُفحص خارجاً ثم تُنقل مع بصمة، وداخلًا سجل حزم محلي؛ الرخص تُحسم قبل اعتماد أداة سحابية فقط.

entries.question: Tell me about a time a production system failed
aliases: tell me about a time a production system failed
what happens if the service goes down
how do you design for failure
tell me about an outage you handled
how do you retry safely
duplicate transaction after timeout
entries.answer_en: In payments we assumed failure would happen. What saved us was a clear log, a known recovery path, and a rule that a retry must not move money twice. I bring that to AI. The model will fail, a tool will time out, the network will drop.
entries.followup_en: So every LLM and tool call is logged, retries use an idempotency key, and nothing irreversible runs without a human. I will not invent a dramatic outage I cannot describe. The lesson is design, not a war story. Timeouts without status checks are how you double-post.
entries.answer_ar: في أنظمة الدفع صممنا بافتراض العطل: سجل واضح ومسار استعادة وإعادة محاولة لا تكرر الأثر، وهذا ما أنقله لأنظمة الذكاء الاصطناعي.

entries.question: Have you managed a GPU server before?
aliases: have you managed a gpu server
have you managed a gpu cluster
do you have experience with cuda and gpu operations
who will install the nvidia drivers
can you own gpu operations
entries.answer_en: Not a GPU cluster, no. I have run on-premise production for years in payment environments: deploy, backup, access, uptime. The new layer is drivers, CUDA, memory planning, and keeping the card busy. I have done the VRAM math. On the first build I would want an infrastructure partner.
entries.followup_en: I would rather say that than discover it during an outage. After the first install I expect to own the runbook: monitoring, image updates, and capacity. I have not used vLLM in production; that would be part of learning the serving layer with that partner.
entries.answer_ar: لم أدِر تجمّع معالجات رسومية، ولدي تشغيل إنتاج معزول لسنوات؛ الطبقة الجديدة CUDA والذاكرة، وأفضّل شريكاً في البناء الأول.

entries.question: Why Redis? What is it used for in AI systems?
aliases: why redis
what is redis
what is redis used for in ai systems
how do you cache llm responses
rate limit llm users
where do you store agent state
entries.answer_en: Redis is a fast in-memory store. In AI I use it to cache repeated answers with a TTL, to rate-limit users, and to hold short-lived session or queue state. The audit log does not live there. That goes to a durable database.
entries.followup_en: A cache key must include the user, the corpus version, and the prompt version, or you serve the wrong department's answer. After a reindex I flush or namespace the cache. Redis is not the source of truth for money or for who approved what.
entries.answer_ar: ريديس ذاكرة سريعة لكاش الأجوبة وحدود المعدل وحالة قصيرة؛ سجل التدقيق لا يُحفظ فيه بل في قاعدة دائمة.

entries.question: Would you use Kubernetes?
aliases: would you use kubernetes
have you used kubernetes
docker compose or kubernetes
how do you scale the deployment
do we need k8s for two gpus
self healing rolling updates
entries.answer_en: I have not used Kubernetes in production. I know it gives scaling, self-healing, and rolling updates. For one or two GPU servers I would start with Docker Compose. Kubernetes is a decision, not a default. I would use it when we need high availability across many machines.
entries.followup_en: GPU scheduling on Kubernetes is its own skill. Adding it on day one slows delivery and needs people who already run it. If the ministry already has a cluster and a platform team, I would follow them rather than invent Compose in a corner.
entries.answer_ar: لم أشغّل كوبرنتس في الإنتاج؛ لخادمين أبدأ بـ Compose، وأستخدم كوبرنتس عندما نحتاج توفراً على عدة أجهزة.

entries.question: How do you make sure the system does not give wrong information in a financial context?
aliases: how do you make sure the system does not give wrong information
how do you prevent wrong answers in finance
how do you make an llm system trustworthy
how do you stop a wrong budget number
can we trust the chatbot on policy
entries.answer_en: The model predicts the next token, not whether the information is true. So I ground answers in retrieved text and allow I do not know. Every number must appear in the source or I block the answer. A person approves anything that becomes an action. We log prompt, answer, and source.
entries.followup_en: Schema checks catch missing citations. They do not catch a well-formed lie. That is why the number-in-source rule is so useful in finance. If retrieval failed, the honest result is abstain, not a fluent maybe. I used teacher approval the same way on BTEC questions.
entries.answer_ar: في المال لا أثق بالنموذج وحده: جواب من النص المسترجع، ولا أعلم إن غاب المصدر، ورفض رقم غير موجود، وموافقة بشرية للأفعال.

entries.question: What are guardrails?
aliases: what are guardrails
what are llm guardrails
define guardrails
what does guardrails mean in ai
is a system prompt a guardrail
input and output filters
what are godrails
what are gardrails
what are god rails
explain guardrails
llm guardrails meaning
entries.answer_en: Guardrails are the checks around the model, before and after it. Before: validate input, catch injection, strip personal data, limit scope. After: force the output shape, check claims against the source, block unsupported answers, require a human for actions. We do not trust the model to be right by itself.
entries.followup_en: A system prompt is the weakest layer. Server-side permissions and schema are stronger. In BTEC the last check is a teacher before save. I would rather a refused answer than a polite wrong one in finance.
entries.answer_ar: الحواجز فحوصات قبل النموذج وبعده: حقن وبيانات شخصية وشكل الخرج ومطابقته للمصدر، وموافقة بشرية قبل أي فعل.

entries.question: How do you build guardrails for an LLM?
aliases: how do you build guardrails for an llm
how would you implement guardrails
what layers of guardrails do you use
how do you put guardrails around an agent
what runs before the model call
how do you limit agent steps
entries.answer_en: Before the model I authenticate, check the schema, strip personal data, and look for injection in user text and in files. Tools are narrow and typed. After the model I validate JSON, require sources, allow I do not know, and stop for a human. I also cap steps, cost, and time, and I log everything.
entries.followup_en: A safety classifier can help. It does not replace server permissions. In the BTEC generator the last rail is teacher approval. For agents, a money tool returns a request object, not a completed transfer. I would fail closed when a check errors, not fail open.
entries.answer_ar: أبني الحواجز بصلاحيات وشكل إدخال، وأدوات ضيقة، ثم تحقق JSON والمصدر، وحدود للخطوات، وسجل كامل، وموافقة بشرية للأثر.

entries.question: How do you know the system is good enough to launch?
aliases: how do you know the system is good enough to launch
how do you evaluate a rag system
how do you measure the quality of an llm application
how do you test an ai system before deployment
what is the launch bar
do you need a golden set
entries.answer_en: I do not launch on a demo feeling. I use a golden set of real questions with the right answer and the clause that should be retrieved. The business writes them. I include questions with no answer, to catch invention. I rerun that set after every change.
entries.followup_en: I split retrieval quality from generation quality. If the right chunk never arrived, a bigger LLM will not save us. I have scored this by hand. I have not used RAGAS as a formal framework. I would use those four scores when we need scale, after we agree the launch bar.
entries.answer_ar: الإطلاق يكون على مجموعة ذهبية من أسئلة العمل مع مصدرها، بما فيها ما لا جواب له، وأعيد تشغيلها بعد كل تغيير.

entries.question: What is a golden dataset?
aliases: what is a golden dataset
what is a golden set
what is a golden test set
how do you build an evaluation set
who writes the evaluation questions
how many questions do you need
entries.answer_en: A golden set is a fixed pack of real questions, the correct answer, and the passage that should be retrieved. Fifty to two hundred is a start. The business writes them. I add questions the files cannot answer, to test I do not know. It does not change without review.
entries.followup_en: I run it after prompt, chunk, embedding, or model changes. If I tune on it every hour, it stops being honest; then I need a second held-out slice. Labels that drift need the same care as training labels. This is the regression test for RAG.
entries.answer_ar: المجموعة الذهبية أسئلة حقيقية ثابتة مع الجواب والمقطع الواجب استرجاعه، يكتبها العمل، وتشمل ما يجب أن يُرفض.

entries.question: How does a faithfulness check actually work?
aliases: how does a faithfulness check work
what is faithfulness in rag
how do you verify the answer is supported by the source
do you split the answer into claims
rule based number check
entries.answer_en: I split the answer into claims: each sentence, each number. For each claim I ask whether the retrieved text supports it. Below a threshold I block and send to a person. In finance I start with a hard rule: every number must appear in the source.
entries.followup_en: A second model can score support, but it can be wrong too. The number rule is boring and strong. I add the model judge on top, not instead. If the claim is a paraphrase of the clause, a judge helps. If it is an amount, string match first.
entries.answer_ar: التحقق من الأمانة يجزّئ الجواب إلى ادعاءات ويطلب سنداً من النص؛ وفي المال أبدأ بقاعدة أن كل رقم يظهر في المصدر.

entries.question: What is LLM-as-a-judge?
aliases: what is llm as a judge
can you use a model to evaluate a model
how do you evaluate answers automatically
is the judge biased
do you calibrate the judge
entries.answer_en: It means a second model scores the first: supported, relevant, complete. That scales beyond what people can read. The judge can be wrong too, so I calibrate it on a human-labelled sample. In finance I still put a number-in-source rule in front. The judge flags. It does not ship money.
entries.followup_en: I would use a different model family when I can, so they do not share the same blind spot. Position bias is real: first answer wins. I shuffle and I keep humans on the golden set. Automatic scores are for regression, not for a single high-risk reply.
entries.answer_ar: القاضي نموذج ثانٍ يقيّم الجواب؛ يُعايَر بعينة بشرية ويُستخدم للرصد لا للقرار المالي، مع قاعدة الأرقام أولاً.

entries.question: What is RAGAS and what do its metrics tell you?
aliases: what is ragas
what metrics do you use to evaluate rag
what are context precision and context recall
what is answer relevancy
have you used ragas
how do you know if retrieval or generation failed
entries.answer_en: RAGAS is a RAG evaluation kit. It splits quality into scores like faithfulness, answer relevancy, context precision, and context recall. If recall is low, I fix chunking or embeddings, not the LLM. I have not used RAGAS in production. I have scored retrieval by hand on real questions.
entries.followup_en: That split is the useful idea even without the library. Precision low means noise in the prompt. Relevancy low means the model ignored the question. I would use RAGAS when the golden set is big enough that hand review does not scale. Until then, a spreadsheet of traces is honest.
entries.answer_ar: RAGAS إطار تقييم للاسترجاع المعزز يفصل خطأ الجلب عن خطأ التوليد؛ لم أستخدمه في الإنتاج وقيّمت يدوياً على أسئلة حقيقية.

entries.question: A supplier sends a file with a hidden line telling the system to rank their offer highest. What happens?
aliases: a supplier sends a file with a hidden line telling the system to rank their offer highest
how do you defend against prompt injection
what if someone hides instructions inside a document
indirect injection in a pdf
should a model rank tenders
entries.answer_en: That is indirect prompt injection. Retrieved text is data to read, never a command. I keep it out of the instruction block. The model has no tool that can rank or award. At worst a human sees a bad summary. For tenders I would not let a model rank offers at all.
entries.followup_en: I would also scan for phrases like ignore previous instructions and for tiny white text. Extraction and comparison tables are fine. The ranking stays with the committee. If the agent could write a score to the database, injection becomes fraud. That is why tools stay read-only here.
entries.answer_ar: هذا حقن غير مباشر؛ نص المورّد بيانات لا أوامر، ولا أداة للترتيب، واللجنة تبقى صاحبة القرار لا النموذج.

entries.question: What is prompt injection?
aliases: what is prompt injection
what is indirect prompt injection
explain prompt injection
what is a prompt injection attack
ignore previous instructions
jailbreak versus injection
entries.answer_en: Prompt injection is text that tries to override the model's instructions. Direct is the user typing ignore your rules. Indirect is a line hidden in a file the system reads. The model cannot fully tell data from commands, so the defense is architecture, not a smarter prompt.
entries.followup_en: Treat untrusted text as data, give no high-effect tools, scan files, keep sensitive decisions with people. Jailbreaks are a cousin: getting the model to drop its safety voice. In RAG, the document channel is the scary one because it bypasses the chat box.
entries.answer_ar: حقن التعليمات نص يحاول تغيير أوامر النموذج، مباشراً من المستخدم أو داخل ملف؛ الدفاع في التصميم لا في جملة أذكى.

entries.question: If an employee acts on a wrong answer from the system, who is responsible?
aliases: if an employee acts on a wrong answer who is responsible
who is responsible if the system is wrong
who is accountable for ai decisions
can we blame the model
how do you make human review fair
entries.answer_en: The organization stays accountable, and the person who approved must be able to check. So the answer shows its source, it can say I do not know, and every step is logged. If we hide the source and speak with fake confidence, we made the human responsible for something they could not verify.
entries.followup_en: That is a design failure, not a user failure. I do not use a slogan here; I mean the UI and the workflow. Propose, review, record. In BTEC the teacher is the decision maker on generated questions. The log is how we reconstruct a dispute later.
entries.answer_ar: المسؤولية تبقى على الجهة وعلى من وافق، بشرط أن يظهر المصدر ويُسمح بلا أعلم ويُسجَّل كل شيء حتى يكون التدقيق ممكناً.

entries.question: Isn't it annoying if the system says 'I do not know' too often?
aliases: isn't it annoying if the system says i do not know too often
what if the system refuses to answer too much
how do you balance safety and usefulness
should the model always give an answer
abstention rate too high
users hate empty answers
listen_for: offer to route to a person
entries.answer_en: It is a trade-off we set with the business. In finance a confident wrong number costs more than a missing answer. A high I-do-not-know rate is a signal: retrieval is weak or the files do not cover the topic. I track it. I do not hide it.
entries.followup_en: The UI can show what we did find and offer to pass the question to a person. Tuning only to reduce abstention trains the model to guess. I would rather fix chunking and coverage. Users forgive 'I don't know' more than a bad figure in a report.
entries.answer_ar: كثرة لا أعلم مزعجة لكنها في المال أهون من رقم واثق خاطئ، وهي مؤشر على ضعف الاسترجاع أو نقص الوثائق.

entries.question: What layers of protection do you put around an LLM?
aliases: what layers of protection do you put around an llm
what are input and output guardrails
how do you architect guardrails
what checks run before and after the model
cheap checks first
defense in depth for llm
entries.answer_en: Cheap checks first. Input: injection, personal data, out-of-scope. Then ground in retrieved text, or abstain. Then Pydantic on the shape. Then a faithfulness pass on claims and numbers. Then a human before any financial effect. One layer is never enough.
entries.followup_en: If the schema fails, I do not skip to the human with raw prose. If retrieval is empty, I do not call the expensive judge. Order saves money and stops leaks. Logs sit beside all of this so we can see which layer fired.
entries.answer_ar: طبقات الحماية تبدأ بالإدخال ثم الاسترجاع أو الامتناع ثم المخطط ثم مطابقة المصدر ثم الإنسان قبل أي أثر مالي.

entries.question: How do you handle personal data in prompts and logs?
aliases: how do you handle personal data in prompts
how do you handle pii
how do you protect personal information in an llm system
what is redaction
do student names go to the model
pii in traces
entries.answer_en: I send the model only what the task needs, never full records. Names and IDs are masked, and we map them back inside our system. Logs are a quiet leak, so they get the same redaction, short retention, and tight access. In BTEC work, student rows did not go to the model.
entries.followup_en: Tools like Presidio can run on-premise. I still review patterns for local ID formats. A trace that stores the raw prompt undoes the API privacy work. For an external model I would be stricter: more masking, or do not call it at all.
entries.answer_ar: أقل بيانات ممكنة للنموذج، مع حجب الأسماء والمعرّفات في الطلبات والسجلات؛ بيانات الطلبة في عملي لم تُرسل للنموذج.

entries.question: What is fine-tuning?
aliases: what is fine tuning
explain fine tuning
how does fine tuning work
when does fine tuning make sense
is uploading pdfs fine tuning
have you fine tuned a model
entries.answer_en: Fine-tuning is extra training that changes some of a pretrained model's weights on selected data. It is not putting files in a vector store. It is not a new prompt. RAG is for knowledge that changes. Fine-tuning is for behavior. I have done only basic fine-tuning.
entries.followup_en: I would use it for a stable report layout or for Arabic finance phrasing we see every day. I would not use it for regulations that move every year. Data quality decides success. A few hundred messy samples will teach the wrong habit.
entries.answer_ar: الضبط الدقيق تحديث لأوزان النموذج على بيانات مختارة لتغيير السلوك، لا لإضافة ملفات؛ المعرفة المتغيّرة مكانها الاسترجاع.

entries.question: What is LoRA?
aliases: what is lora
what is parameter efficient fine tuning
what is peft
how does lora work
why not full fine tune
multiple adapters on one base
entries.answer_en: LoRA is low-rank adaptation. We freeze the big model and train small extra matrices, called adapters. That needs far less GPU memory. I can keep several adapters on one base model. It is the usual parameter-efficient fine-tune. I understand it. I have not run large training jobs in production.
entries.followup_en: Full fine-tuning rewrites huge weight files and is easy to overfit. LoRA is how most teams actually specialize a 7B model. Serving then means loading the right adapter. My CV's fine-tuning basics stop here: method and when I would pick it, not a training cluster I owned.

entries.question: What is idempotency and why does it matter?
aliases: what is idempotency
why does idempotency matter
how do you make retries safe
how do you prevent duplicate transactions
the request timed out did it pay
idempotency key
entries.answer_en: Idempotency means doing the same logical request twice does not double the effect. Money moves once. In practice: a stable request id, a stored status that blocks duplicates, and a status check after a drop before we try again. A plain retry is not safe.
entries.followup_en: I learned this on KNET payment work. Agents need it too: if a tool times out, the next call must not create a second ticket or a second transfer. GET can be naturally idempotent. POST needs a key. Timeouts without that key are how finance incidents start.
entries.answer_ar: عدم التكرار يعني أن إعادة نفس الطلب لا تكرر الأثر؛ مفتاح ثابت وفحص الحالة قبل إعادة المحاولة، وهذا حاسم للمال وللوكلاء.

entries.question: How do you measure and improve latency?

how do you monitor performance
why is rag slow
should we stream the tokens
where is the time spent
entries.answer_en: I split time into retrieval, generation, and waiting on other services. I watch p95, not only the average, because the slow tail is what users remember. Then I cache, stream the first tokens, route easy questions to a small model, and cap output length.
entries.followup_en: I have not used vLLM in production; I would use it to batch GPU work. Extra chunks in the prompt are hidden latency. I instrument cost and errors next to latency so we do not speed up by dropping safety checks. Fix the stage the trace points to.

entries.answer_en: p95 is the time that 95 percent of requests beat. If p95 is four seconds, one request in twenty is slower than that. I track it instead of the mean because the mean hides pain. For a live assistant I set the target on p95.

entries.question: The RAG system gives a wrong answer. How do you debug it?

the answer is wrong, where do you look first
how do you find where rag fails
did the right chunk reach the model
trace one rag request
entries.answer_en: I split retrieval from generation. Did the right chunk even reach the model? If not, I fix files, chunking, or embeddings. No prompt tweak will help. If the chunk was there and the answer is still wrong, I look at the prompt, the model, and the schema. I trace one request end to end.
entries.followup_en: I keep the retrieved text, the exact prompt, and the raw output. Then I rerun the golden set so the fix does not break yesterday's cases. Empty retrieval should abstain. A confident answer with the wrong clause in context is a ranking problem; hybrid search or a reranker is the next test. I have not used a cross-encoder in production.

Q363. How do you decide between RAG, fine-tuning, and traditional ML? English: Traditional ML: Tabular data, classification, regression, small data. I often combine them: RAG for knowledge + fine-tuning for tone. Arabic: تعلم الآلة التقليدي: البيانات الجدولية، التصنيف، الانحدار، البيانات الصغيرة. entries.question: What is a reflection or self-critique step in an agent, and when is it worth it?
aliases: what is a reflection step in an agent
what is self critique in an agent loop
when would you add a critic step to an agent
is reflexion worth the tokens
should an agent check its own output
what is an evaluator or critic agent
entries.answer_en: Reflection means the agent looks at its own output against the goal and tries again before anything leaves the system. It pays when the failure is visible from the output itself, like a wrong JSON shape, a claim with no source, or a broken plan. It does not pay when you have no way to judge the output, because then you are just spending tokens to sound more confident.
entries.followup_en: I prefer a cheap deterministic check first. In the Ministry flow the critic is Pydantic and the retrieval evidence, not a second model: if the schema fails I retry, if there is no retrieved text I stop. A model critic is the fallback for things a schema cannot see, and it needs a hard cap on iterations, otherwise cost and latency grow with no bound. If a reflection loop cannot fail, it is decoration.
entries.answer_ar: الانعكاس يعني أن الوكيل ينظر إلى مخرجه مقابل الهدف ويحاول مجدداً قبل أن يخرج شيء من النظام. يستحق حين يكون الخلل ظاهراً في المخرج نفسه، كشكل JSON خاطئ أو ادعاء بلا مصدر أو خطة مكسورة. ولا يستحق حين لا تملك طريقة للحكم على المخرج، فتكون تنفق توكنات ليبدو أكثر ثقة.

entries.question: What kinds of memory does an agent need, and what do you keep versus recompute?
aliases: what kinds of memory does an agent need
difference between short term and long term agent memory
what is episodic memory in an agent
what do you store between agent steps
how do you manage agent context over a long session
when do you summarize the conversation instead of keeping it
entries.answer_en: Short-term memory is the working state of one task: the goal, the steps taken, tool results. Long-term is what survives the task: facts about the user or the domain that you look up later. I keep what I cannot rebuild, like a decision, an approval, or a tool result that cost money. I recompute what is cheap and I retrieve documents rather than memorising them.
entries.followup_en: Context is a budget, not a container. When a session grows I summarise the older turns and keep the decisions verbatim, because a compressed decision is worth more than a compressed greeting. Long-term memory needs the same care as any store: who can read it, how it is deleted, and whether a fact is still true. That is why in the Ministry work student personal data does not go to the model at all, and the unit text is retrieved fresh instead of remembered.
entries.answer_ar: الذاكرة قصيرة المدى هي حالة العمل لمهمة واحدة: الهدف والخطوات المنفّذة ونتائج الأدوات. وطويلة المدى ما يبقى بعد المهمة: حقائق عن المستخدم أو المجال تُستدعى لاحقاً. أحتفظ بما لا أستطيع إعادة بنائه، كقرار أو موافقة أو نتيجة أداة كلّفت مالاً. وأعيد حساب الرخيص، وأسترجع المستندات بدل حفظها.
